label: input token p at original-phase position >= 3, scaled by position
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase when the input token is the letter p and the step index is t >= 3. Every such step is active (dev precision 1.0, F1 0.994). Magnitude grows steadily with position: about 0.25 of max at t=3, about 0.5 at t=4, about 0.65 at t=5, about 0.8 at t=6, about 0.93 at t=7, and about 1.0 at t=8. This holds whether or not p already appeared earlier in the sequence, and it does not depend on L or on surrounding tokens. It never fires on p at t=0..1 (only a handful of very weak activations at t=2), never on the delimiter step, and never in the copy phase, including when p is fed back as input or is the token being output. Activations on other input tokens are negligible (a few hundred weak hits on e).

issues: None of the claims could be refuted. On the test split the predicate has precision 1.0 (0 false positives), recall 0.989, F1 0.994 and mass recall 0.9996.
All 671 test misses hold 0.0% of activation mass. They are very weak hits (0.01-0.03 of max), mostly on e at t=8, plus about 200 dev hits at t=2. This is scattered noise, not a systematic class.
The phase breakdown confirms 0 activations on the delimiter step and in the copy phase, even when p is the input or the output token there.

Magnitude grows with position as described. Top examples are about 1.0 at t=8. Lower-quartile examples show about 0.24-0.26 at t=3, 0.48-0.52 at t=4, 0.65-0.70 at t=5, 0.81 at t=6, and 0.93-0.95 at t=7, even when p repeats. The original phase has no t=9 step (the maximum L is 9), so t=8 is the peak by construction.

There is no dependence on prev_tok, prev2_tok or first_tok (flat lift), and precision 1.0 holds across repeated p (in_count up to 4). The L trend only reflects that longer sequences have more t>=3 slots.
